material_findings.reasoning: The final treats approval fatigue as sufficient to reject the entire approved-rewrite mechanism. The frozen P4 requires maintainer approval and does not specify automatic application, bypassing PR review, or bulk acceptance. GitHub documents deliberate suggestion application on a PR compare branch as a tracked commit, including provenance, and also documents delegating review feedback to Copilot. Thus suggested changes need not bypass docs-as-code review. Report-only triage is a permissible recommendation, but changing the approved object to triage and requiring per-passage human re-authoring are added constraints, not a correction required by the brief. The final retains labeled proposal attachments and a normal PR path, so the loss is narrower than N1; its categorical rejection and assertion of no false rejection nevertheless remain materially unsupported. This is not a finding that every approval workflow is safe, or that a portal must directly write files.

material_findings.reasoning: Antora resource IDs can carry an explicit version, but when a different component is named and its version coordinate is omitted, resolution selects that component’s latest version. A reader of an older component release can consequently be linked to a newer other-component passage. Naming version coordinates elsewhere or proposing a later citation probe does not make the governing claim true; it requires explicit applicability qualification. The finding concerns default resolution, not whether Antora is a viable platform.

validation_assessment.judgment: Controlled stale index plus known conflicting release fixtures and schema assertions discriminate version leaks. Top-hit-only checks are narrower than all chunks used in an answer; they are useful initial probes, not exhaustive answer guarantees. Not executed.

Hosted reachability and local-crawler dry-run separate technical failure and eligibility. Neither fixes the organization’s visibility policy; “settles U1” is too strong if read literally. Not executed.
Representative Local Search vs Pagefind corpus measures index bytes, configured isolation and multilingual behavior. README support is not a runtime scale/isolation witness. Not executed.

Explicit CJK/IME/diacritic fixtures with a bounded locale matrix improve discrimination. IME commit is post-v1.5.2 main code; need actual selected release applicability before a runtime witness. Not executed.

Holding engine constant for threshold sweeps, with separate cross-engine arms, avoids attributing an engine change to a 5/9 vs 4/7 setting. Identifiers have independent expected exact-match truth. Not executed.

Recency-sort placement/order-swap fixtures should expose bucket ordering and relevance/recency trade-off. Results must be expected labeled relevance, not a zero exit or ported other-engine ranking rule. Not executed.

Twenty sampled quotes with exact/normalized identity rule, version and permalink checks provide a passage oracle. Manual identity needs a predefined reviewer rule. “FIX at build” is a future prerequisite, not proof already present. Not executed.

Authored custom rules followed by known injected conflicts provide recall truth. A git-clean state cannot alone distinguish all unauthorized transient/external writes; broad semantic contradictions remain outside basic lint. Not executed.

Must-preserve fields and fixed recall threshold improve export fidelity. Removing second-system import means this cannot alone discriminate authoring lock-in (N1-M4). It is not a scientific round-trip simply because several output files are emitted. Not executed.
